solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pounds distributed: 59? Could be

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so the letters of the word before are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
59 in Roman numerals is L (50) plus IX (9)

explanation.surface: A sum of money is shared out, and someone wonders whether it comes to fifty-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue is both the wordplay (the scrambled word plus the Roman numeral) and a fair description of SPONDULIX, a slang word for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondulix is old slang for money, and pounds handed out to someone are exactly that kind of cash.

clue.text: Owlish cry, making short work of literature exercise in school

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here within the abbreviation for an educational establishment

parts.note: Sch is the abbreviation for school
crit is short for criticism, an exercise in literary analysis

explanation.surface: A hoot like an owl's cuts short a pupil's literature lesson at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making short work of' looks like an idiom for finishing fast; here 'short' just clips the critical exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A scritch is a shrill screech, the sort of noise a barn owl gives.

clue.text: Bulldog accompanies one to forage for food locally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Oxford slang for a proctor, the official whose attendants were called bulldogs
second meaning: a dialect verb, to search around for food

explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a bulldog is a proctor's attendant, so the one a bulldog accompanies is a proctor. 'Locally' flags a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: University slang shortens proctor this way, and in dialect the same word means to scrounge or hunt about for provisions.

clue.text: Not old, dodgy ticker stopped early? Feature of lynching

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for new, the opposite of old

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or faulty, so the letters of the heart word are jumbled
stopped early means cut off before the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man's dicky heart gave out early, which is the point of a lynching.
explanation.walkthrough: Ticker is slang for the heart, which makes the grim surface work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynch mobs hanged victims with a rope, grimly called a necktie, as in the phrase necktie party.

clue.text: Entry passage deserted, room's cluttered

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for deserted

indicators.note: a cluttered space is untidy and jumbled, so the letters of the possessive word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The hallway is empty while the room itself is full of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dromos is the passageway leading into an ancient Greek tomb or temple.

clue.text: Group, myself included, about to swear, showing right to be in court (11, two words)

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps around the curse word

parts.note: a lot is a group of items or people
cuss is informal for curse or swear
and means with, included alongside
I is the speaker, oneself

explanation.surface: A crowd, including me, was about to curse, thereby proving its entitlement to be heard in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Locus standi is a Latin legal phrase used in British courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus standi is the legal standing that entitles a party to be heard before a court.

clue.text: Place for students brought up revolutionary, hardened

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: uni is short for university
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone raised at university became a radical and grew tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inured to hardship has become accustomed and toughened by it.

clue.text: Anatomical parts? There's a lump on one

parts.note: lob is a dialect word for a lump
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking whether some body parts are affected, the answer is yes: one has a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'a on b' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobi is the Latin plural of lobus, a lobe, a rounded section of an organ like the brain or lung.

clue.text: Rendered lustful, I learn with cads, dissolute

indicators.note: dissolute means loose and debauched, and loosened letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they have learned to be sensual from hanging around with debauched scoundrels.
explanation.definitionFit: To carnalise is to make sensual or fleshly, so a person made this way has been aroused to bodily desire.

clue.text: Deploying this initially, police range in it?

definitions.text: Deploying this initially, police range in it?

indicators.note: in it says the reworked item is placed inside the letters just taken
to police is to control and sort out, so the word after it is put into a new order
initially points to the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: first letter of the word
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Police fan out over an area using this sweeping search.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: 'police' reads as the force doing the searching, but it also orders the letters of 'range'; the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a systematic police search covering a whole area, the net trawling through it.

clue.text: Love of the French yields such lyrical efforts

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
des is French for of the (plural)

explanation.surface: The French way of loving produces romantic verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, usually addressed to a subject in an elevated style.

clue.text: News broadcasters en—— were of use to French writers once?

parts.words: News broadcasters en—— were of use to French writers once?
parts.note: surface reading: some old-time announcers were apparently helpful to French authors

parts.words: en—— were of use to French writers once?
parts.note: setter's reading: put EN before the answer and you get the French word for inkwells, which writers dipped their pens in

explanation.walkthrough: The gap stands for the answer itself: EN plus it makes encriers, French for inkstands, which French writers really did use before pens held their own ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Town officials who shouted out public announcements in the street were the original spreaders of news.

clue.text: In an indecent manner

parts.note: surface reading: a plain description of rude behaviour
setter's reading: just the definition, since this is the word competitors write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle prints only a straight definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without propriety or decorum, in an unseemly or offensive way, is behaving indecently.

clue.text: Installed in car, say, a boon possibly on road

indicators.note: possibly suggests the two words before it are only one possible version, so their letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Rd is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A device fitted in a car, perhaps a satnav, proves a real blessing out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment built into a vehicle, like a computer or camera, is described as being carried aboard it.

clue.text: Light-hearted film from Monaco, set in space

indicators.note: something set in a place is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move
MC is Monaco's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: A cheerful movie from the principality of Monaco, set out among the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in space' reads like a science-fiction setting, but space is just a room into which Monaco's code goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A romcom, short for romantic comedy, is a light, amusing film about people falling in love.

clue.text: Bird returns, clutching part of her underwear — and shades

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so the bird's letters wrap around the item of clothing
something that returns goes back the way it came, so the bird's name is read from right to left

parts.note: the emu is the large flightless Australian bird
a bra is an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A bird comes back holding a piece of a woman's lingerie, along with some sunglasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbrae are shadows, especially the darkest central parts cast in an eclipse, so the plural matches shades.

clue.text: Twinkling gays? They're often in evidence at kirk funerals

definitions.text: They're often in evidence at kirk funerals

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as in the twinkling of an eye
urning is an old term for a homosexual man

explanation.surface: Glittering gay men are, oddly, a common sight at Scottish church funerals.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirk is the Scottish word for church; in Scots usage mournings are the black clothes worn for a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournings are black garments worn as a sign of grief, naturally seen when Scots gather to bury someone.

clue.text: Plates set out with tortoni, something Khoikhoi relish (13, two words)

indicators.note: things set out are arranged afresh, so the letters of the two food words are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; tortoni is an Italian ice cream

explanation.surface: Dishes laid out with an Italian ice-cream dessert make a treat the Khoikhoi people enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Khoikhoi are a people of southern Africa; the plant's starchy rootstock, also called Hottentot bread, was eaten by them.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise plant is a South African yam whose edible tuber served as food for the Khoikhoi.

clue.text: Strong creature that, but old one, stressed finally

parts.note: the ox is proverbially strong
yt is an archaic written abbreviation of that
taken as written

explanation.surface: A powerful beast, but an elderly one, is put under strain at last.
explanation.walkthrough: In old manuscripts y stood for the letter thorn, so yt was a scribal form of that.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an oxytone word carries its accent on the last syllable.

clue.text: Local? Slope round — it's to do with classification system

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the slope word goes around the pub word

parts.note: to lean is to slope or tilt
a local is a British pub near where you live

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood pub on a hillside turns out to be connected with taxonomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local?' looks like Azed's usual dialect flag, but here it is the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Linnean relates to Carl Linnaeus, the Swedish botanist who devised the binomial scheme for naming organisms.

clue.text: Nice summer drawn in, cut short, is wavering

indicators.note: drawn in means pulled inside, so the season word goes within the word for curt
cut short also tells you to lop the final letter off the combined result, so these words work twice

parts.note: terse means brief, clipped
été is French for summer, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: A summer on the Riviera that ends early leaves someone uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' does double duty: it gives the word for curt and then says to drop the last letter of the whole. 'Nice' is the French city, flagging a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble unsteadily, and a verb in the third person matches 'is wavering'.

clue.text: Hals represented current monarch to give a stony face

indicators.note: represented means depicted in another form, so the painter's name is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; Frans Hals was a Dutch painter
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the reigning monarch in 2016

explanation.surface: The painter Frans Hals portrayed the reigning queen with a deadpan expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stony face' looks like an expressionless look, but it is the dressed stone facing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashler, a variant of ashlar, is squared building stone used as a smooth facing on walls.

clue.text: One's shot small part with actor/model in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the previous piece, so the model's name goes within

parts.note: pt is the abbreviation for part
Elle Macpherson is an Australian model who has also acted

explanation.surface: Someone gets a chance at a minor role in a film featuring a model-turned-actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's shot' reads as someone's opportunity, but it means one piece of shot, the small balls fired from a shotgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a single ball of lead shot, so each one of the shot is this.

clue.text: Rock publicity stunt, right? Later featured in web location

indicators.note: a thing featured in something appears inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: hype is extravagant publicity
R is the standard abbreviation for right
a website is a location on the web
then means afterwards, at a later time

explanation.surface: A rock band's publicity stunt, which later appears on a website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music in the surface, but it is the definition: the answer is a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersthenite is an igneous stone made largely of the mineral hypersthene, so it is a type of rock.

clue.text: Tug (using old-fashioned power) a US hamlet reconditioned

indicators.note: an engine that is reconditioned is taken apart and rebuilt, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tugboat with an old-fashioned engine is refurbished in a small American village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tug' looks like a boat in the surface; here it is the verb, to pull, and the bracket says the pulling uses steam.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam-haul is to draw a train or load by steam locomotion, an outdated source of motive force.

clue.text: Sea ——-free? It makes surface seem tidied up

definitions.text: Sea ——-free? It makes surface seem tidied up

indicators.note: tidied up means put in a fresh order, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

parts.note: the letters around the gap, which must be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: If the sea were clear of floating muck, its surface would look clean.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the phrase with the answer in the gap uses exactly the letters of 'surface seem', so taking away SEA and FREE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is the film of dirt that floats on top of water, so removing it leaves the surface tidy.

clue.text: What a baby needs in one of the later months (not now)

definitions.text: one of the later months (not now)

parts.note: taken as written
a bib is what a baby wears at mealtimes

explanation.surface: Something an infant requires in one of the coming months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not now' says the month name is no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Abib was the old Hebrew name of a month in spring, later replaced by Nisan.

clue.text: What happens when name's forgotten? Ask!

indicators.note: a forgotten name is left out, so the abbreviation for name is dropped from the word

parts.note: an event is something that happens
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what to do when they cannot remember a person's name, and is told simply to enquire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ask' looks like the verb, but it is an old dialect noun for a newt, and so is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Evet and ask are both old dialect names for the newt, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Eye's caught by small room missing last wall bracket

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so the first piece goes within the second
missing last tells you the final letter of the word for a small room is dropped

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
orb is a poetic word for an eye

explanation.surface: Someone's eye is drawn to a tiny room that has lost its last wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing last wall' seems a single phrase, but 'missing last' works on the room, and 'wall bracket' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corbel is a projecting block of stone or timber jutting from a wall to support a beam or shelf.

clue.text: Local hillside circled by vehicle eventually

indicators.note: circled by means surrounded, so the answer lies enclosed within the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood slope is finally ringed round by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word, a regular Azed device; CLEEVE is a regional term for a steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleeve is an English dialect word for a cliff or steep hillside, found in many place names.

clue.text: Shorebird, English, first to last showing no sign of age?

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is moved to the end, rotating the letters along

parts.note: the dunlin is a small wading bird of the shore
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A wading bird, an English one, comes in first, then last, and still looks youthful.
explanation.definitionFit: A face without wrinkles is unlined, so it betrays no ageing.

clue.text: Head of showbiz gang? That's you, right now

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Ralph ..., who founded and ran the Scouts' Gang Show
second meaning: the person reading this clue

explanation.walkthrough: The Gang Show was a British Scout variety revue created by Ralph Reader, so its leader shares a surname with anyone looking at the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever is scanning this clue at this moment is literally the one perusing the text, and the Gang Show founder bore that surname.

clue.text: They move with tides (tend first going astray)

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of the bracketed words wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Things carried along by the sea, with the reminder to look after them before they wander off.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is two words, drift nets, so the single-word enumeration is arguable.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift nets are fishing nets left floating so they are carried by currents rather than anchored.
